title: Wright-Patterson: ATIC, the Foreign Technology Division and Moon Dust
notes: Added: not in Appendix T. The Air Force technical-intelligence line at Wright-Patterson (ATIC; the Foreign Technology Division, constituted 1 July 1961; NASIC) and the Moon Dust and Blue Fly recovery projects form a clear group in the 1947-69 community. Canon cluster 10 (Goldwater, LeMay and the Blue Room) is a research gap inside this topic. ATIC became the Aerospace Technical Intelligence Center in 1959 and was discontinued on 1 July 1961 (do not write 'ATIC became FTD').

lead.text: Wright-Patterson Air Force Base in Ohio housed the Air Force's foreign materiel exploitation organisation and its UFO projects SIGN, GRUDGE and Blue Book, under Air Materiel Command intelligence and then ATIC. From 1966 the Foreign Technology Division held the Blue Book effort there by regulation, and recovered foreign materiel was airlifted there under Project BLUE FLY.

summary.text: The lineage is a succession, not a string of renamings: the Air Technical Intelligence Center was established on 21 May 1951, redesignated the Aerospace Technical Intelligence Center in 1959 and discontinued on 1 July 1961, when a newly constituted Foreign Technology Division absorbed its mission. The board carries the later step to the National Air and Space Intelligence Center at Tier 2.
On UFOs the office at Wright-Patterson was the terminal analyst: ATIC under AFR 200-2 from 1953, which also issued Special Report No. 14 in 1955, and FTD under AFR 80-17 from 1966.

On recovery, the 1127th USAF Field Activities Group ran Project BLUE FLY and Project MOON DUST together under its Foreign Materiel Program, with FTD exploitation teams and airlift to Wright-Patterson.

The base is also where later custody allegations point, from Tom DeLonge's 2016 email about Roswell material to accounts attached to a former base commander, Arthur Exon, and the Air Force has denied in writing that any extraterrestrial visitors or equipment were ever there.

record.text: AFR 200-2 of 26 August 1953 designates ATIC at Wright-Patterson as the Air Force activity responsible for analysing information and evidence, and the 1954 edition makes it the terminal authority once Air Defense Command and the 4602d Air Intelligence Service Squadron have exhausted identification. Neither edition mentions Blue Book, which was a project inside ATIC.
ATIC issued Project Blue Book Special Report No. 14 on 5 May 1955 under Project 10073.

AARO's 2024 history records that Ruppelt created a contract with Battelle, informally called Project BEAR, to give scientific support to Project GRUDGE, and that Battelle released its report under the cover of ATIC to keep its anonymity.

ATIC and the Wright Air Development Center issued TR-AC-47, the Project Silver Bug report, on 15 February 1955, declassified on 29 March 1995. It presents technical data on A. V. Roe Canada's Project Y2, a flat-riser, in order to correct the distorted picture in earlier releases, says the design should in no way be linked with flying saucer stories because of its appearance, and dates the Air Force development track from a technical requirement of 13 August 1954.

AFR 80-17 of 19 September 1966 assigns the Blue Book effort to FTD at Wright-Patterson, requires FTD to analyse every report not identified at base level and to write the final case report on each, and makes the Deputy Chief of Staff for Research and Development responsible for the programme overall.

The Air Force Scientific Advisory Board committee of March 1966 called FTD the cognizant Air Force agency that collates information on UFO sightings and monitors investigations, recommended that it keep those responsibilities, and put the programme's resources at only one officer, a sergeant and a secretary.

The 1127th's history for January to June 1967, classified SECRET with struck-through special access markings, lists Project BLUE FLY, MIG-17 Exploitation and Project MOON DUST under its Foreign Materiel Program. Under BLUE FLY it records FTD Detachment 3 exploiting three MIG-21s that crashed in Jordan and the airlift of about three tons of parts and armament to Wright-Patterson, and a Joint Chiefs extension of F/AD-I priority for short-notice BLUE FLY airlift contingencies.

The companion history of the Assistant Chief of Staff, Intelligence, for July to December 1967 covers the 1127th as a subordinate unit under Col. Rudolph C. Koller Jr., with authorised strength rising from 220 to 249.

MOON DUST is officially described as the recovery of objects and debris from space vehicles that survived re-entry, and State Department files on it have been released under FOIA. The unit histories record notifications of deorbit: 37 Soviet space objects in the first half of 1967, and 49 Soviet and 17 US objects in the second.
Leslie Kean's FOIA request that led to Kean v. NASA named Project Moon Dust among the records sought.
The base's own published history lists Col. Arthur E. Exon as installation commander from August 1964, succeeded in December 1965, and names him nowhere else.

The Operation UPSHOT-KNOTHOLE Project 3.1 report names Eric H. Wang as Chief of the Special Studies Office, Installations Division, Air Materiel Command, and technical and scientific monitor for the Air Force programme, whose responsibility moved to Blast Effects Research at the Wright Air Development Center on 15 November 1954; a 1960 report has him as Chief, Structures Division, at the Air Force Special Weapons Center, Kirtland.
A letter of 24 November 1947 from Air Materiel Command intelligence to the Chief of Staff on the flying disc problem survives as a scan.
Maj. Gen. William N. McCasland's Air Force biography describes him as Commander, Air Force Research Laboratory, at Wright-Patterson.

claimed.text: Tom DeLonge wrote to John Podesta on 25 January 2016 that when Roswell crashed "they shipped it to the laboratory at Wright Patterson Air Force Base", and that General McCasland had been in charge of that laboratory until a couple of years before and had helped assemble DeLonge's advisory team. The record shows that DeLonge wrote this, not that it happened.

Whitley Strieber said on the Danny Jones Podcast in September 2024 that Exon, whom he called a general and the commander of Wright-Patterson, and Strieber's uncle had told him of 1947 material at the installation. The Air Force's record gives Exon's rank in the post as colonel and carries none of the account.

The stories of Eric Wang running special projects at Wright-Patterson reached the public by one route: Matthew Pines traced them to William Steinman's book on the 1948 Aztec crash, and Pines's link to Henry Kissinger is his own reading of the initials H-A-K. Michels later retold Steinman's account of an obituary and of Wang's widow, none of which the board has opened.

A serving NASIC intelligence officer with Top Secret clearance, writing as Jonathan Grey, backed Grusch on the record in The Debrief in June 2023 with the words "The non-human intelligence phenomenon is real. We are not alone."

McCoy, as Chief of Intelligence at Air Materiel Command, is described in Ruppelt's book and the Condon Report as heading the organisation that would have received any recovered material and as SIGN's operational supervisor.

On the board's reading, Wright-Patterson is the institutional address of any legacy recovery effort, because the Air Force gave UFOs to the organisation whose mission was taking foreign hardware apart, and its 1947 to 1951 files have had no comprehensive declassification review. The board also infers that BLUE FLY made the base the custody terminus for recovered material, and that MOON DUST's tasking outlived Blue Book.

The board further infers that ending Blue Book left the Foreign Technology Division's collection channels intact, and that the Air Force Research Laboratory, co-located with NASIC, is the most probable modern home of any exploitation work begun there. Both are stated inferences.

contested.text: The Air Force's January 1985 fact sheet from Wright-Patterson states that there are not now, nor ever have been, any extraterrestrial visitors or equipment on the base.
The MOON DUST figures often quoted as recoveries are notifications of deorbit received, not objects recovered; neither unit history counts a recovery.

The records disagree on the Battelle contract: AARO calls it Project BEAR and says the report was completed in late 1954, while the Project Stork status reports identify the contract as AF-19741, PPS-100, from 31 March 1952, and Special Report No. 14 is dated 5 May 1955.

Wang's documented work is blast effects on structures: nothing in the test reports or the 1960 Kirtland report touches unidentified aerial phenomena, recovered materiel, Kissinger or Viktor Schauberger, and no document supporting an Austrian birth was found. The office's printed name is the Special Studies Office, not an Office of Special Studies.

McCasland's Special Programs post of 2009 to 2011 was in the acquisition under secretary's office, not the intelligence office to which DIA addressed its 2009 memo declining the AAWSAP special access program request, so nothing places him in that decision; the email's General McCasland is matched to him by name only.
A common claim that AFR 200-2 routed reports to ATIC rather than to Blue Book is a category error, since Blue Book was a project inside ATIC.

questions: When was the 1127th USAF Field Activities Group activated and inactivated, and where was it stationed? No lineage record has been found.
Did MOON DUST ever recover anything that the released histories count, what was the United States figure that is illegible on page 30 of the 1967 history, and was the tasking ever formally ended?
Have Air Materiel Command's T-2 intelligence files for 1947 to 1951 ever been reviewed for declassification, and where are they held?
What does the untranscribed 24 November 1947 letter from AMC intelligence to the Chief of Staff say?
The board carries nothing yet on the Blue Room story told of Barry Goldwater and Curtis LeMay: what is its earliest dated artefact, and who first told it?
Who is Jonathan Grey, and did NASIC take any action after his statement?
